name: Texaf Bilembo
funding: Texaf, listed on Euronext Brussels, is founder and head sponsor of the centre. Its income is 85% Kinshasa real estate, 12% a sandstone quarry and 3% digital.
watch: Texaf is 62.9% held by Société Financière Africaine and 10% by the Cha family. Bilembo covers over 1,000 m² of exhibition and workshop space.
records_note: Posts a 2025 activity report and an undated partner logo strip; no accounts or board named, though founder Texaf publishes its own audited accounts.

name: Laongo Granite Sculpture Symposium
funding: Burkina Faso's culture ministry organises it and pays professional artists' fees, flights and stay, per its 2024 call for applications. No other funder is named.
watch: Founded 1989 by Siriki Ky, 35 km from Ouagadougou. The 15th edition runs 2 to 23 November 2026 under President Traoré's patronage.
records_note: Run by the culture ministry with no site of its own; the ministry site is down, so reports, accounts and board could not be checked.

name: National Arts Festival
funding: Eastern Cape government, Sarah Baartman District Municipality, National Lottery Commission, Standard Bank. National government gave R5.5 million for 2022 to 2024, nothing in 2025, a smaller grant in 2026.
watch: Minister McKenzie says it lost an open call. A January 2026 petition of 302 artists cites the cut among his refusals to renew funding.
records_note: Names its eleven-member board and management, and two presenting sponsors in text with logos for the rest; no annual reports or accounts found.

name: Javett Art Centre at the University of Pretoria (Javett-UP)
funding: University of Pretoria gave the land and funding. The Javett Foundation funded construction and pledged ten years of annual gifts for running costs and an endowment.
watch: Opened September 2019. An independent trust runs it. Michael Javett founded the Unisec Group, later sold to Standard Bank, and Tolux, now Brait.
records_note: Posts one annual artistic report, for 2023, with no figures; no accounts, funder list or board names on its site.

name: Art D'Égypte
funding: Private firm of Nadine Abdel Ghaffar. Egypt's foreign and tourism ministries and UNESCO sponsor Forever Is Now. Partners: LMD, Suez Canal Bank, BMW (2026); TotalEnergies, Afreximbank (2024).
watch: In October 2026 a petition of 500 to 700 signatories made it drop sculptor Bernar Venet over Israeli ties; artists and galleries withdrew.
why_flagged: Private firm of Nadine Abdel Ghaffar. Egypt's foreign and tourism ministries and UNESCO sponsor Forever Is Now. Partners: LMD, Suez Canal Bank, BMW (2026); TotalEnergies, Afreximbank (2024).
records_note: It posts no reports or accounts; the site shows four logos of ministries and UNESCO, undated, and lists a three-person team but no board.

name: G.A.S. Foundation (Guest Artists Space)
funding: Primarily funded by the Yinka Shonibare Foundation at its 2019 launch. Donors include Terra Foundation, Deutsche Bank, Afreximbank, Still Earth Holdings, British Council and Pro Helvetia.
watch: Founded 2019 by Yinka Shonibare, who started the London residency Guest Projects. Patron Still Earth Holdings owns drilling contractor Tirex, an oil-services supplier.
records_note: Posts two impact reports (2022 to mid-2025), a named donor list and its trustees; accounts are filed by its UK parent, the Yinka Shonibare Foundation.

name: blaxTARLINES KUMASI
funding: Art network and incubator tied to the KNUST painting and sculpture department in Kumasi.
watch: Ranked 69 in ArtReview's 2025 Power 100 and invited to the 2026 Venice Biennale main exhibition.
records_note: No blaxTARLINES website was found; Wikipedia lists none and no source names a funder, report, accounts or board.

name: Musée Boribana
funding: Founded with private money by Boubacar Koné and actress CCH Pounder; Koné gave it to the Senegalese state in December 2014.
watch: Ngor museum of contemporary African art with artist studios and a residency. A conservator from the Ministry of Culture took office in March 2015.
records_note: The ministry page on Boribana gives its history and 2014 state handover but no budget, reports, accounts, funders or board.

name: Contemporary Art Museum of the Kasbah
funding: Run by the National Foundation of Museums. Restoration and design cost 13 million dirhams; the Wilaya of Tangier supervised it, with the Ministry of Culture, APDN and the Foundation contributing.
watch: Opened in December 2021 in the former Kasbah prison to mark the Foundation's tenth anniversary. Opening show: The School of the North.
records_note: Publishes nothing itself; its operator, the National Foundation of Museums, posts laws and an org chart image but no reports, accounts, donors or board names.
